notes: Summary: Glacier Helm is an industrial automation company (robotic fleet + edge telemetry) evaluating Redwood Private VPC for LLM-based operational assistants and anomaly summarization. Primary constraints: strict data residency (US + EU partitions), no public ingress to inference nodes, customer-managed keys (AWS KMS / CloudHSM), and audit-grade logging shipped to Splunk. They want an architecture where inference runtime sits in customer VPC (private subnets) with outbound-only egress via NAT/egress gateway and explicit allow-listing of Redwood control-plane endpoints. Require cross-account IAM roles and STS-based short-lived creds. Must support VPC endpoints (Interface/PrivateLink) and Transit Gateway peering for multi-region fabric. Architecture asks: provide 2 topology options: (A) single-account deployment with per-cluster private subnets and customer-managed KMS keys + CloudHSM wrapper, (B) cross-account model where Redwood hosts control-plane in a private tenant VPC and inference nodes are owned by customer — both must avoid public IPs on inference hosts and expose only internal ALB or NLB with mTLS. Inbound: limited to AWS PrivateLink or customer bastion. Outbound: allowed to specific S3/Secrets endpoints and Redwood artifact registries via NAT and VPC endpoints. Regions: prefer us-east-1 for pilot, eu-west-1 for EU-residency workloads.
